FOR BEVIN CARTER

A practical first experiment.

A proposed approach, scope, and path to a small pilot.

01 / APPROACH

Prove the measurement first.

Use WebGazer to estimate screen gaze from a standard webcam. Run nine-point calibration, a separate five-target validation, then a short reading activity. Review a spatial heatmap, sample availability, and time within broad content regions. Export raw samples and validation results.

Use measured pixel error to judge suitability for broad regions. Do not claim word-level tracking, attention scores, learning outcomes, or clinical validity.

02 / TIMELINE

Two to three weeks to a pilot.

Days 1–3: prototype review, define devices and measurement criteria.
Days 4–7: improve calibration and test camera, glasses, lighting, and movement conditions.
Days 8–10: adult usability sessions, exports, defect fixes.
Optional week 3: supervised pilot and findings.

This working demo is the starting deliverable. Human webcam reliability testing remains to be completed.

03 / BUDGET

US$2,000–4,000

Planning estimate for pilot hardening: 40–80 engineering hours at an assumed US$50/hour. A further 20–40 hours for a facilitated pilot would be US$1,000–2,000.

No paid tracking API is required for this implementation. Hosting, participant compensation, specialist hardware, and commercial licensing review are excluded. These are estimates, not a quote or a record of charges.

04 / INPUTS WHEN READY

What would help next.

A representative learning activity; intended adult participants and devices; the research question and acceptable error; approved Faraday logo, colours, and typography; and an agreed consent, retention, and export process.

No inputs are needed to present this demo. The visual identity is a bespoke provisional direction, pending official brand assets.

A REPEATABLE FIRST TEST

Keep the experiment honest.

01. Prepare

Use a desktop browser, webcam, steady lighting, and a comfortable fixed position. Explain that estimates can be inaccurate. Obtain permission before enabling the camera. Do not include names or sensitive learning material.

02. Calibrate

Look at each orange target while clicking it five times. Keep your eyes on the target. Nine points train the estimate; rehearsal mode uses the pointer and does not train a gaze model.

03. Validate separately

Look at each of five new targets for three seconds. Validation samples are never added to calibration. Report median error in pixels, 90th-percentile error, target coverage, and sample availability. The provisional gate is median error ≤120 px with ≥70% sample availability and ≥10 samples per target; this is a prototype heuristic, not a validated standard.

04. Observe and review

Read for 45 seconds; pause or stop at any time. Do not scroll or resize. Treat the heatmap as sample density, not proven fixations. Missing samples and offscreen estimates remain visible in the report. Recheck accuracy after movement or between activities.

Data & privacy

Sessions stay in memory until you export or clear them. No video is recorded. Face-tracking assets are served by this site. Camera frames and session samples stay in this browser; they are not uploaded by this app. Downloaded exports stay on your device until you delete them.

Known limits

A consumer webcam is sensitive to face position, glasses, lighting, device performance, and browser support. Do not infer engagement, emotion, disability, or comprehension. An instrument can capture gaze patterns without explaining why they occurred.

For more precise research, compare against dedicated eye-tracking hardware and an independently designed validation protocol.
